Subject: KEK derivation validation + operator logs — SIG follow-up

Jordan,

Thanks again for the walkthrough earlier. As part of our SIG intake and upcoming SOC 2 audit appendix we need a compact evidence set covering how Redwood derives and rotates Key Encryption Keys (KEKs) used to wrap tenant data keys. Please provide the following:

- KEK derivation parameters (KDF algorithm, salt handling, info/context strings, iteration counts) used in production for tenant BYOK and Redwood-managed keys.
- A redacted operator shift log extract that shows HSM operator activities for a 24-hour window around a rotation event (include timestamps, operator IDs, and high-level action tags; redaction of personal IDs is fine).
- HSM attestation or vendor-signed cert for the HSM firmware + FIPS module version currently in our cluster.
- Brief narrative on the canary rotation process (how you validate successful unwrap/wrap across replicas) and the planned maintenance window for the upcoming rotation.

Deliverables can be uploaded to the shared Drive link we already provisioned. Also let me know if you prefer to demo the rotation in a short call rather than send logs.

Appreciate a reply by COB Friday (US PT).

—Alice
Alice Turner
Director, Security Engineering — Acme Financial

Alice — thanks for the clear checklist. We can provide everything requested; below is what I can deliver by Friday and a few clarifying questions.

Planned deliverables (ETA: 2026-11-13 16:00 PT):
- kek-derivation-parameters.txt — concise dump of KDF config used in our runtime (algorithm, HKDF info strings, salt lifecycle, derived key lengths).
- operator-shiftlog-sample.csv — redacted shift log with action tags (rotate, unwrap, wrap, snapshot, audit-export).
- hsm-attestation-20260930.pdf — vendor attestation we already have (will include certificate chain).
- brief rotation-narrative.txt — step-by-step canary rotation checklist and rollback criteria.

Clarifying items:
1) For the operator logs, do you need the raw operator IDs or is pseudonymous operator IDs acceptable? We plan to pseudonymize (operator-47) and keep mapping offline.
2) For the KEK derivation: we use HKDF-SHA384 with per-tenant salt + a site-wide pepper derived from the HSM root. Does Acme need the pepper provenance or is confirming it is HSM-derived sufficient?
3) Are you requesting the full audit trail for one rotation, or a sampling covering both pre/post checksums and successful unwrap verification?

If helpful, we can demo the canary rotation next Tuesday (30 minutes) and show the wrap/unwrap validation across three replicas.

Regards,

Jordan Blake

Forwarding the attestation and the KDF parameter dump. Notes inline:

--- Forwarded message attached ---

From: HSM Vendor <attestations@hsmvendor.example>
Date: 2026-09-30
Subject: Redwood cluster HSM attestation
Attachment: hsm-attestation-20260930.pdf

Attachment: kek-derivation-parameters.txt (redwood internal) — excerpt below:
- KDF: HKDF-SHA384
- Salt: per-tenant, 32 bytes, rotate on tenant rekey action; salts are stored encrypted in the keystore (wrapped by KEK).
- Pepper: 64-bit site pepper derived from HSM-root using NIST SP800-108 KDF in counter mode; never stored in plaintext outside HSM.
- Info/context: "redwood:kek:v1" plus tenant-id when deriving tenant-specific KEK.
- Derived KEK length: 256 bits; output truncated for AES-GCM-256 wrapping.
- Iterations: HKDF uses standard extract/expand with SHA-384; additional iteration-based stretching is not used (we rely on HSM KDF properties).

Operational note: KEKs are rotated via a canary-first rollout: one replica performs an unwrap/wrap cycle with the new KEK and the resulting wrapped tenant keys are validated via checksum and replayed traffic in staging before cluster-wide promotion. Canary rotation failures trigger automatic rollback to previous KEK and an operator alert.

I attached the vendor attestation PDF and the parameter dump to this thread.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Principal Applied Cryptography Engineer
Redwood Inference

Thanks — that looks good. A couple of follow-ups:

- Pseudonymous operator IDs are fine; we will expect a non-production justification for mapping storage.
- For the pepper provenance, confirming HSM-derived is sufficient — but we will need the vendor attestation (PDF) signed and the certificate chain.
- For the rotation sample, we want a full pre/post verification set: pre-rotation checksum, unwrap/wrap success status, and post-rotation integrity check. If you can mark the sample with UTC timestamps that helps our ingest pipeline.

Also, would Redwood be willing to run a short canary rotation in a meeting where Acme observers are in view-only? We'll need a 30-minute window with low-traffic tenant simulation. If yes, propose a date/time (US PT) and we will provide observers.

Appended: DocuSign link for a brief NDA supplement to allow observers to see pseudonymous operator IDs: https://docusign.example/ACME-NDA-REDWOOD-2026
